chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Sulami, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Muhammad! Peace conveys its greetings to you and says: I did not create the seven heavens and what is in them, and the seven earths and what is on them, nor did I create any place greater than the Rukn and the Maqam. And if a servant supplicated to Me from the time I created the heavens and the earth, then met Me denying the Wilayah of Ali, I would surely cast him headlong into Saqar (Hell).'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ وَالْمَقَامُ: The Rukn and the Maqam (sacred spots in the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of denying the Wilayah of Imam Ali despite lifelong worship?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* underscores the centrality of Imam Ali’s Wilayah in Shia theology by linking it directly to divine acceptance of worship. It presents a striking theological paradox: even a lifetime of devotion is rendered void if accompanied by the denial of Ali’s authority, illustrating that Wilayah is the key to salvation. The mention of the Rukn and Maqam serves to anchor this spiritual reality in the physical sanctity of the Kaaba, reinforcing the unity of cosmic and earthly worship.
